<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915520_theRebbe_327" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915520_theRebbe_327__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that thought grasps only revelations, while the desire of the heart (ratzono shel lev) grasps Atzmus itself, analogous to a son's essential love for his father.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And the point of the explanation in this</t>
    <t s="2">(in the maamar13)</t>
    <t s="3">is based on what is stated in the Zohar14:</t>
    <t s="4">"No thought can grasp You at all,</t>
    <t s="5">but He is grasped by the desire of the heart."</t>
    <t s="6">For thought</t>
    <t s="7">[the comprehension of Binah and also of Chochmah which is above the comprehension of Binah,</t>
    <t s="8">including also the vision of Chochmah15]</t>
    <t s="9">grasps only revelations, not Atzmus,</t>
    <t s="10">and through the desire of the heart one grasps Atzmus.</t>
    <t s="11">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="12">that in love there are two levels in general:</t>
    <t s="13">love based on reason and understanding,</t>
    <t s="14">and essential love that stems from the essence of the soul which is connected to Atzmus.</t>
    <t s="15">Like the love of a son for his father, which is an essential love from the essence of the son for the essence of the father.</t>
    <t s="16">And this love is called "the desire of the heart."</t>
    <t s="17">And this is "He is grasped by the desire of the heart,"</t>
    <t s="18">for just as the son arouses the essence of the father,</t>
    <t s="19">for when the son cries out "Abba!" the father is stirred in his entire being,</t>
    <t s="20">so too in the analogy,</t>
    <t s="21">the essential love that stems from the essence of the soul grasps Atzmus.</t>
    <t s="22">And this is that "the ultimate and primary purpose of wisdom is repentance and good deeds"16,</t>
    <t s="23">for wisdom grasps only revelations</t>
    <t s="24">(as above),</t>
    <t s="25">and in order to grasp Atzmus it is through repentance and good deeds.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section questions whether the explanation that repentance and good deeds grasp Atzmus only elevates them above wisdom, but the maamar's context suggests it also explains why the essence of Torah is repentance and good deeds.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it must be understood,</t>
    <t s="1">that this matter</t>
    <t s="2">(that wisdom grasps revelations,</t>
    <t s="3">and in order to grasp Atzmus it is through repentance and good deeds)</t>
    <t s="4">only explains the superiority of repentance and good deeds over wisdom.</t>
    <t s="5">For although in the level of the faculties of the human soul, the study of Torah is more elevated than repentance and good deeds,</t>
    <t s="6">for the study of Torah is in his intellect,</t>
    <t s="7">and repentance and good deeds are in the emotions of the heart and the power of action</t>
    <t s="8">[repentance in the emotions of the heart17,</t>
    <t s="9">and good deeds in the power of action],</t>
    <t s="10">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="11">there is an advantage in repentance and good deeds, that specifically through them one grasps Atzmus.</t>
    <t s="12">But this explanation is seemingly only according to the interpretation that "the ultimate purpose of wisdom" is the ultimate elevation of wisdom.</t>
    <t s="13">For since through repentance and good deeds one grasps Atzmus,</t>
    <t s="14">therefore,</t>
    <t s="15">through the fact that wisdom leads to repentance and good deeds,</t>
    <t s="16">an elevation is also effected in wisdom</t>
    <t s="17">[like the statement "great is study that leads to action"18,</t>
    <t s="18">for through the study leading to action, it is greater than it is in itself].</t>
    <t s="19">And from the continuation of the topics in the maamar it seems,</t>
    <t s="20">that this matter</t>
    <t s="21">(that wisdom grasps revelations,</t>
    <t s="22">and in order to grasp Atzmus it is through repentance and good deeds)</t>
    <t s="23">is also an explanation of the fact that the essence of Torah is repentance and good deeds.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the Zohar's statement "He is grasped by the desire of the heart" has two aspects: grasping within the desire itself, and the desire as a prerequisite for fulfilling mitzvos, through which Atzmus is grasped with complete self-nullification.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And it will be understood by prefacing,</t>
    <t s="2">that what is stated in the maamar in continuation of the matter of "He is grasped by the desire of the heart," that through repentance and good deeds one grasps Atzmus,</t>
    <t s="3">it can be said based on what is explained in many places19,</t>
    <t s="4">that the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos that follows the desire of the heart is on a more elevated level</t>
    <t s="5">(as will be explained below).</t>
    <t s="6">And based on this it can be said,</t>
    <t s="7">that what is stated in the Zohar, "He is grasped by the desire of the heart,"</t>
    <t s="8">there are two matters in this:</t>
    <t s="9">that He is grasped in the desire of the heart itself,</t>
    <t s="10">and that the desire of the heart is a prerequisite for the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos, in which Atzmus is actually grasped.</t>
    <t s="11">That is,</t>
    <t s="12">that in order to grasp Atzmus itself, it is</t>
    <t s="13">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="14">through the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos20,</t>
    <t s="15">except that this grasping of Atzmus through the performance of mitzvos is when the action is performed with self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="16">and the self-nullification in the performance of mitzvos is when the love that brings about the fulfillment of mitzvos is an essential love above reason and understanding,</t>
    <t s="17">the desire of the heart.</t>
    <t s="18">For when the love21</t>
    <t s="19">[during prayer]</t>
    <t s="20">is based on reason and understanding,</t>
    <t s="21">the fulfillment of mitzvos</t>
    <t s="22">[throughout the entire day]</t>
    <t s="23">is in order to draw down a revelation of G-dliness.</t>
    <t s="24">And even when the love is through contemplation of the wondrous nature of Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="25">through which one comes to the great love of "Who22</t>
    <t s="26">is for me in heaven?"</t>
    <t s="27">that he does not desire any revelations, only Atzmus23,</t>
    <t s="28">there is still a request in his fulfillment of mitzvos</t>
    <t s="29">(throughout the entire day),</t>
    <t s="30">to draw down a revelation of the Atzmus of Ein Sof.</t>
    <t s="31">But the fulfillment of mitzvos that follows the arousal of essential love</t>
    <t s="32">(the desire of the heart)</t>
    <t s="33">is without any request</t>
    <t s="34">[even the request for drawing down a revelation of the Atzmus of Ein Sof]</t>
    <t s="35">and only to fulfill His will,</t>
    <t s="36">in the manner of accepting the yoke.</t>
    <t s="37">For the self-nullification in the fulfillment of mitzvos in this manner is even greater than the self-nullification in the desire of the heart24,</t>
    <t s="38">and through the fulfillment of mitzvos in this manner, there is a drawing down of Atzmus.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
